rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ibâk” means a slave's fleeing from his master.
rows.anchor: “İbâk” bir kölenin efendisinden firar etmesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus left in anger without waiting for divine permission, which is why the verse calls his departure ibâk.
rows.anchor: öfkelenip taraf-ı ilâhîden izin gözlemeksizin çıkmış olduğundan “ibâk” tâbir buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi transmits the People of the Book's account: sent to Nineveh, overwhelmed by its wickedness, Yunus fled toward Tarshish via Jaffa and boarded a ship caught in a storm.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî tefsirinde der ki: “Yûnus aleyhisselâm hakkında ehl-i kitâbın kitaplarında mezkur olan şudur

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: In that account, sailors cast lots to identify the cause of the storm; the lot fell to Yunus, who confessed his flight and told them to throw him overboard.
rows.anchor: gelin bu şer bize kimin sebebiyle geldi bilmek için kura atalım’ dediler, kura attılar Yûnus’a düştü.

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: The sailors tried to return to shore, then threw Yunus in; the sea calmed, a great fish swallowed him, and he remained inside for three days and nights praying.
rows.anchor: nihâyet Yûnus’u tuttular, gemide bulunanların necâtı için denize attılar, derhâl deniz durdu

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: In Alusi's account God released Yunus ashore and sent him back to warn Nineveh of destruction in three days.
rows.anchor: Allah azze ve celle ona ‘kalk, Ninova’ya[^6] var

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: The Ninevites, including their king and animals, fasted and repented; God showed mercy and withheld punishment.
rows.anchor: Ninova[^9] ricâli Allah teâlâ’ya iman ettiler ve oruç nidâ ettiler

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: The account continues with Yunus wishing for death, sheltering outside the city, and grieving when a gourd that shaded him withered; God asks why he pities the gourd but not populous Nineveh.
rows.anchor: “ya sen o hiç üzerine yorulmadığın, bakıp büyütmediğin, belki bir gecede bitip bir gecede helâk olan kabağa acırsın da

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi says he relayed the account for information despite points in it that conflict with the truth.
rows.anchor: bunda hakka muhalif noktalar bulunmakla beraber ıttılâ‘hâsıl olmak için nakleyledim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalili urges attention to Qur'anic delicacy: unlike the transmitted tale's order, the Qur'an places Yunus's release from grief and his gourd after his sick emergence from the fish, ending with his people's beneficial faith.
rows.anchor: balığın karnından[^13] hasta olarak çıkarılması akibinde olarak anlatmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since punishment was promised for unbelief, there is no sense in Yunus grieving that God spared the believing people as if the prophet had proved false; his grief may instead date to his initial anger and flight.
rows.anchor: Azab iman etmediklerinden dolayı mev‘ud olduğu için kavmi iman ettikten sonra azab

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus fled to a fully laden ship; the sailors drew lots, and he was among those who lost and were cast out.
rows.anchor: Hani o dolu gemiye kaçmıştı {فَسَاهَمَ} da sehim, kura atışmıştı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mudhaddin means those defeated in the lots and expelled from the ship; though some say Yunus threw himself, the wording's apparent sense does not support that, but he may have consented.
rows.anchor: burada kendi kendini attı diye bir söz varsa da ٱلْمُدْحَضِينَ tâbirinin zâhirine muvâfık değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish immediately took Yunus as a morsel, that is, swallowed him.
rows.anchor: Derhâl balık onu lokma etti, yani yuttu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muleem describes him as blameworthy in that state, blaming himself and regretting what he had done.
rows.anchor: o hâlde ki melâmette idi, kendini levm ediyordu, pişman oluyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus was already among those who frequently glorified God; in the darkness he called, “There is no god but You; glory be to You; I was among the wrongdoers.”
rows.anchor: öteden beri Allah’ı tesbih ile çok zikrederdi, bu zulümâtta da لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

words: لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had Yunus not been one of the frequent glorifiers, he would have remained in the fish until the day people are resurrected; he did not remain there.
rows.anchor: ba‘s olunacakları güne kadar elbette onun karnında kalırdı lâkin kalmadı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cast Yunus onto an open, empty expanse while he was sick.
rows.anchor: hemen Biz onu alana, açık, boş bir sahaya fırlattık {وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌۭ} o hâlde ki hasta idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqtin is a gourd-family plant: stemless, quick-growing, spreading and branching, with large leaves suited to provide shade.
rows.anchor: Gövdesiz, çabuk biter, çok çatallanır, uzar ve yaprakları büyük olduğundan gölgeliğe kābiliyetli bir ağaç

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although it has no trunk, the spreading plant is called a tree because its branches rise up.
rows.anchor: sâkı olmadığı hâlde buna ağaç denilmesi çatallanıp yükselebilmesi itibariyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gourd grew over Yunus's head to shelter him while he was ill; Elmalili also allows that this may indicate a simple arrangement.
rows.anchor: başında bu kabağın bitmesi çıktığı sırada hasta hâlinde bir siper olmak için idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus was sent back to the place from which he had fled, to a population of one hundred thousand.
rows.anchor: onu, yani Yûnus’u yüz bine gönderdik yani kaçtığı yere tekrar gönderildi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Or more” means they were numerous though not immense, and able to grow; it may signal that their population increased between Yunus's two missions.
rows.anchor: Bu tâbir iki irsal arasında tezâyüd bile vâki‘olduğuna işarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people believed and were allowed to live until their appointed time; although faith in despair normally gives no benefit, this was granted to Yunus's people.
rows.anchor: Îmân-ı ye’s fâide vermezken bu suretle kavm-i Yûnus’a verdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in “ask them” summarizes the warnings and stories since 37:73–74, including Yunus, then directs Muhammad to question the idolaters without shrinking from prophetic hardship.
rows.anchor: emrinden buraya kadar tafsil olunan kıssaları bir telhis ederek demek olur ki şimdi bunlara atf-ı nazar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes the unequal division that assigns daughters to God and sons to the idolaters: “What kind of apportionment is this?”
rows.anchor: Rabbine kızlar, onlara oğullar öyle mi! Bu ne biçim taksim?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab polytheists including Juhayna, Banu Salama, Khuza'a and Banu Mulayh called angels God's daughters, though they themselves disliked having daughters.
rows.anchor: “melekler Allah’ın kızlarıdır[^20]” diyorlardı, hâlbuki kendilerinin kız evlâtları olsa istemiyorlardı.

words: أَمْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ إِنَٰثًۭا وَهُمْ شَٰهِدُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they excuse the claim by saying “daughters” means female creatures, the rebuttal asks whether they witnessed the angels being created female.
rows.anchor: Yoksa Biz melâikeyi dişi olarak yaratmışız da onlar şâhidler mi imiş?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine declaration exposes their lies and invalidates their doctrine; testimony about an obvious falsehood and contradiction cannot be accepted.
rows.anchor: doğrudan doğru taraf-ı ilâhîden yalancılıklarını ilan ile mezheblerini ibtal

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fabricated a kinship between God and jinn, implying a relation or partnership in divinity; this accusation is attached to their claim that God has offspring.
rows.anchor: Bir de Allah ile cinler beyninde bir neseb uydurdular. Bu cümle لَيَقُولُونَ وَلَدَ ٱللَّهُ kavli üzerine mâtuftur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from direct address to speaking of them in the third person warns that the vileness of their words makes them unfit for direct address.
rows.anchor: Hitabdan yine bu suretle gıyâba geçilmesi sözlerinin şenâ‘atinden dolayı hitâba kābiliyetleri olmadığını bir ihtardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here jinn has the broad sense of hidden beings, including angels, metaphysical powers and all spiritual beings.
rows.anchor: “cin” meleklere dahi şâmil olan e‘am mânaya

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some polytheists called Satan God's brother and angels His daughters; others worshipped spirits as mediators and intercessors, or divided good and evil between them.
rows.anchor: birtakımları da “rûhânîlerin, cinlerin, meleklerin Allah’a münasebeti, yakınlığı vardır. Biz onların vesâtati olmaksızın Allah’a yaklaşamayız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalili refers readers to his exegesis of 6:100 and 6:112 for fuller discussion of associating jinn with God and devils among jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i En‘âm’da وَجَعَلُوا۟ لِلَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ ٱلْجِنَّ [6/100], وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِىٍّ عَدُوًّۭا شَيَٰطِينَ ٱلْإِنسِ وَٱلْجِنِّ [6/112] âyetlerinin tefsîrinde buraya dair tafsîlât geçmişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirits they associate with God, especially angels, know the claimed kinship is false; the liars who invented it will be brought to Hell, while God is beyond their descriptions.
rows.anchor: o neseb isnad ettikleri rûhânîler ale’l-husus melâike

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above the attributes the polytheists ascribe to Him; the angels glorify and declare Him transcendent.
rows.anchor: Allah, onların isnad ettikleri vasıflardan münezzeh sübhândır. Bilirler, böyle tesbih ile tenzih ederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even Iblis admits that he was created from fire and declares himself free of the polytheists, thereby disavowing their ascriptions to God.
rows.anchor: diye mahlûkiyetini itiraf eden İblis bile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's sincerely chosen servants are the exception: they make no such attribution and therefore are not brought to punishment.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın ihlâs ile seçilen kulları başka onlar öyle isnadda bulunmazlar ve onun için azâba da ihzar olunmazlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels say that people and their idols or devils cannot lead anyone astray from God except those destined to burn in Hell; they cannot corrupt God's chosen servants.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın ihlâs ile seçilen kullarını bozamazsınız. Şu da o bilen cinlerin, yani melâikenin sözlerindendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each angel has a known, fixed station for worship before God and cannot go beyond its appointed limit.
rows.anchor: her birimizin Allah teâlâ’ya ubûdiyet için durduğumuz mâlum bir makamı, muayyen bir haddi vardır ki onu geçemeyiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels form ranks and glorify God, declaring Him free of attributes unworthy of His majesty and categorically rejecting claims of offspring or kinship.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh veled, neseb gibi isnadları kat‘iyyen reddederiz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the following clause, wa-inna is the shortened form of inna.
rows.anchor: وَإِنَّ’nin muhaffefidir. Yani ve gerçek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh had said that with a revealed reminder like earlier peoples possessed they would become God's chosen servants; when the Qur'an, the best reminder, came, they rejected it.
rows.anchor: fakat olunca ona küfrettiler ihlâs ile sarılmak şöyle dursun küfrettiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will later see the outcome of their disbelief.
rows.anchor: artık ileride bilecekler küfürlerinin âkıbeti neye varacağını görecekler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's prior decree promises support for His messengers and victory for His armies; prophetic missions will ultimately prevail, making this a promise to Muhammad and a warning to opponents.
rows.anchor: Peygamberlerin hikmet-i irsalleri âkıbet tahakkuk edecek, davaları zaferi kazanacaktır. Burada bu kelime-i ilâhiye Peygamber’e vaad ve muhaliflerine va‘îd siyâkındadır.

words: سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ ٱلْعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close declares Muhammad's mighty Lord, who sent him as a messenger and promised certain victory, exalted above the disbelievers' deficient descriptions; His promise cannot fail or be resisted.
rows.anchor: seni terbiye edip risaletle gönderen ve o kat‘î nusret ve galebeyi vaad buyurmuş olup vaadinde hulf etmesine veya kuvvet ü kudretine karşı gelinmesine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Peace is upon Muhammad and all messengers, whose victory was decreed from eternity; praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and the closing verse is especially comprehensive.
rows.anchor: bir de selâm, o mürselîne mansûriyetleri ezelde mukadder olan sana ve yukarıda bir kısmının isimleri geçmiş olan bütün peygamberlere

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A report Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from al-Shaʿbi says that whoever wants a full measure of reward on Judgment Day should say something when leaving a gathering; the excerpt ends before giving the formula.
rows.anchor: İbn Ebî Hâtim’in Şa‘bî’den tahric eylediği bir hadiste Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurmuştur ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israf usually means spending money excessively, but more broadly it is exceeding bounds in any act; here it includes wronging one's own soul through excessive sin.
rows.anchor: “İsrâf” mal sarfında meşhur ise de insanın yaptığı herhangi bir fiilde haddini aşmaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿalā incorporates the sense of committing a crime against oneself into the phrase.
rows.anchor: Burada cinayet mânası da tazmin olunarak عَلَىٰٓ ile sılalanmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though called the Qur'an's most hopeful verse, its hope is meant to urge even the greatest sinners to repent immediately, not to encourage sin.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetin Kur’an’da en ümidli âyet olduğu söylenir. Bununla beraber dikkat edilmek lâzım gelir ki bu ümid, günaha teşvik için değil

rows.speaker: Atâ b. Yesâr
rows.claim: Atā ibn Yasār reports that the verse was revealed in Medina concerning Wahshi, the killer of Hamza.
rows.anchor: Atâ b. Yesâr’dan[^1] olan rivayete göre

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that tortured converts Ayyaash, Walid ibn Walid and others who had renounced Islam received the verse through Umar's handwritten letter and then returned to Islam and emigrated.
rows.anchor: İbn Ömer’den rivayet olunduğuna göre de demiştir ki: “Ayyaş b. Ebî Rebî‘a ve Velîd b. Velîd ve daha birkaç nefer Müslüman olmuşlardı.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Meccans asked how they could convert after idolatry and murder if Muhammad claimed such sins were unforgiven; God then revealed this verse.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan rivayet olunduğuna göre de Mekkeliler şöyle demişler: “Muhammed zu‘mediyor ki putlara tapan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the reported occasion concerns unbelievers entering Islam, the verse also includes sinful believers' repentance, all the more so.
rows.anchor: sebeb-i nüzul kâfirlerin islâmı meselesi ise de mefhum âsîlerin tevbesine de şâmil olduğunda şüphe yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God does not forgive associating partners with Him means unrepented shirk; repentance makes forgiveness possible.
rows.anchor: âyeti mûcebince şirkin mağfiret olunmaması tevbe edilmediği takdirdedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call is to seek refuge in the Lord through repentance and sincere submission before punishment arrives; after that, there is no escape.
rows.anchor: başınıza azab gelmeden evvel tevbe ile Rabbinize dehâlet edin ve ona hâlis müslümanlık yapın, sonra kurtulamazsınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning to repent before punishment means faith adopted in despair will not benefit a person.
rows.anchor: Azab size gelmezden evvel buyurulması da îmân-ı ye’sin fâide vermeyeceğini anlatır.

words: وَٱتَّبِعُوٓا۟ أَحْسَنَ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before sudden punishment arrives unnoticed, one must sincerely submit to God and follow and apply the best of what He has revealed.
rows.anchor: Haberiniz olmayarak ansızın başınıza azab gelmeden evvel hâlis müslüman olun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A soul will lament its failures toward God and admit that it had been among those who mocked.
rows.anchor: Eyvah, Allah yanında yaptığım eksikliklerden dolayı hasretime bak, doğrusu ben eğlenenlerden idim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “that a soul should say” means “lest a soul say,” expressing the aim of preventing this regretful speech.
rows.anchor: Bir nefis diyeceği için[^1] yani dememek için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another soul will say that if God had guided it, it would have been among the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: Allah bana yolunu gösterse idi her hâlde ben müttakīlerden olurdum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On seeing the punishment, a soul will wish for another return so that it could become one of the good-doers.
rows.anchor: Bana bir geri dönmek olsa idi de muhsinlerden olsa idim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply is that God's signs came, but the person denied them, acted arrogantly and became an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: Hayır sana âyetlerim geldi de onlara yalan dedin, kibretmek istedin ve kâfirlerden oldun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Day of Resurrection, those who lied about God will have darkened faces, and Hell is the abode of the arrogant.
rows.anchor: Allah’a karşı o yalan söyleyenlerin yüzleri kararmıştır; cehennemde değil mi mevkiʿi mütekebbirlerin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will rescue the protected God-fearing as He wills; no harm will touch them and they will not grieve.
rows.anchor: Korunan müttakīleri ise Allah muradlarınca necâta çıkarır, onlara fenalık dokunmaz ve onlar değildir mahzun olacaklar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God controls all things, or watches over them and carries out their interests and responsibilities.
rows.anchor: Yani üzerlerinde tasarruf kendisine ait olan yahut görüp gözetecek, maslahat veya mes’ûliyetlerini tatbik eyleyecek olan ancak O’dur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalili links God's guardianship over everything with 39:41, where Muhammad is told he is not the people's guardian.
rows.anchor: tâ yukarıdaki وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِوَكِيلٍ hitâbına mukabildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqālīd is the plural of miqlīd or miqlād, meaning locks or keys; it is also said to be the Arabicized “key” or the plural of iqlīd.
rows.anchor: cem‘idir ki kilit veya anahtar demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The locks or keys signify the treasures of the heavens and earth and God's unrestricted power to dispose of them as He wills.
rows.anchor: Burada kilit veya anahtardan maksat yer ve gök hazineleri ve onlarda dilediği gibi tasarruf etmektir.
